subject: legend of continuous variable as categorical variable

messages.author: 4f6f5f995ee31178
messages.subject: legend of continuous variable as categorical variable
parts:
Hi!

Using
http://dl.dropbox.com/u/3180464/vthcal2MIDAScal2m.rda

I'm doing:
qplot(DN,fill=glass,alpha=I(0.2),group=glass,data=vthcal2MIDAScal2m,geom=c("density"))+facet_grid(Image~.)+opts(title="Set
2")
qplot(DN,fill=temperature,alpha=I(0.2),group=temperature,data=vthcal2MIDAScal2m,geom=c("density"))+facet_grid(Image~.)+opts(title="Set
2")

actually, each histogram of DNs corresponds to a glass with a unique
temperature, so I would like the second qplot() but having
the actual temperatures of the 6 glasses in the legend. I think the
legend gets as it is because temperature is a continuous variable.
Is there any way I can set the values of the legend in the second plot
to match the ones of the glasses? (c(13.0,15.3,17.9,18.9,19.6,22.4)) ?

Thanks
Agus

messages.subject: RE: legend of continuous variable as categorical variable
parts:

"?as.factor" or "?factor"

messages.author: 4f6f5f995ee31178
messages.subject: Re: legend of continuous variable as categorical variable
parts:
Thanks for your answer.
I had tried with as. character(temperature), I should have mentioned
it, which yields a similar result.
The problem is that what I would like is keeping the continuous color
scheme, having a color bar in which
the ticks and labels are set in accordance to the values of the
glasses. That is, the ticks and labels of the legend
would not be regularly distributed (as by default), but in the places
that correspond to the glasses. This would be best for
a continuous variable (temperature).
But factor(temperature) is a good second option.

Agus
